risks: The guard is static (AST), not behavioural. A use case could call authorize and then read data belonging to another operation. The ordering test pins gate-before-any-statement-that-reads, which catches the realistic defect, but this is a structural proof, not a runtime one; the use-case tests remain the behavioural evidence.

GATED_ROUTERS deliberately lists only ops and policies. agents/notes routers are owner-scoped and gated by the authorization provider instead. A future platform-wide router added outside those two modules would not be covered until it is listed -- the test cannot discover routers it was not told about. Widening it would require a decision about which routers are platform-wide, which is a domain judgement rather than a syntactic one.

KNOWN_OPERATOR_OPERATIONS is resolved by walking module constants. If the registry is rewritten to build its set dynamically (a comprehension over a function call, say), the registry test's `assert registry` guard fires loudly rather than passing vacuously -- but the fix would be to teach the resolver, not to weaken the assertion.
`git rev-parse origin/<branch>` reads a frozen snapshot in this clone (remote.origin.fetch maps only refs/heads/main). Use `git ls-remote`.
